verdicts.reason: Both look like the original shrunk into a 320x50 strip. A two-line headline plus a pill CTA are crammed into the centre-left, the headline sits almost flush with the top edge, the CTA text is tiny, and large dead orange areas fill both sides, so neither layout reads left to right. The two are near-identical; B sits marginally lower, but not enough to split them.

In A the headline block is pushed right (centred around x≈220) while the CTA sits further left (around x≈170), so they share no axis; the CTA reads as stranded and the whole left 40% of the canvas is empty. B keeps the headline and CTA in one tight centre-left group. B still has a tiny CTA, a cramped top margin and empty flanks, but it is more coherent.

Both leave about 100px of empty orange on the left and jam the text block against the top edge, with an undersized CTA. A breaks the headline into a wider two-line block ('Bubbles, botanicals and / a little sunshine.'), which suits the banner shape a bit better. B's narrower block leaves more dead space on the right, though A's CTA sits slightly offset from the headline's left edge.

The two are practically identical: the headline is centred over a left-aligned pill CTA, so the block's edges don't share an alignment. The CTA label is tiny and barely legible at banner size, the headline touches the top, and large empty areas sit on both sides. Neither has been rearranged for a leaderboard format.
